$comment: ★ SHIPS THE TWO FUNCTIONS, DELIBERATELY SHIPS NO MIB CONSTANTS — the two halves have DIFFERENT reasons and neither is an oversight. Neutral shipped <sys/sysctl.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. ★★ (1) WHY THE FUNCTIONS ARE NOW HERE — THIS FILE USED TO ARGUE THE OPPOSITE AND THE ARGUMENT WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. The previous version shipped NO `symbols` and justified it thus: the functions 'are already shipped ... re-declaring either here would plant a SECOND eager import of the same symbol for no gain'. THAT IS WRONG IN EFFECT, because DESCRIPTOR VISIBILITY IS PER-HEADER: a descriptor SHADOWS the real header TOTALLY, and the angle-include funnel resolves DESCRIPTOR FIRST (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp:205-224 — priority 1 Descriptor, 2 Source, 3 NotFound; it keys on descriptor-FILE existence ALONE, and an existing-but-format-unavailable descriptor STILL returns Descriptor rather than falling through to a real header). So a TU that includes <sys/sysctl.h> sees THIS FILE AND NOTHING ELSE — unistd.json's rows are not in scope for it, however much they exist. MEASURED 2026-08-05 in the staged tree (/home/rafael/src/sqlite/bld-dss/sqlite3.c, re-checked this cycle rather than inherited): `#include <sys/sysctl.h>` at :28198, the call `sysctlbyname("hw.ncpu", &cpuCount, &len, NULL, 0)` at :28388, and the nearest later <unistd.h> at :31315 (inside a conditional) with the first unconditional one at :39635 — BOTH thousands of lines AFTER the call, so neither can rescue it. MEASURED both directions with the real CLI the same day: <sys/sysctl.h> + a sysctlbyname call failed `error[S0001] got sysctlbyname` on BOTH macho targets, while the identical call under <unistd.h> compiled rc=0 — the header, not the symbol, was the variable. NOTE the line numbers above are true for the tree staged on that date only; the harness re-pulls upstream every run, so re-measure before re-quoting. What does NOT drift is the ORDER, and the order is the whole defect. ★ (2) WHY A BYTE-IDENTICAL DUPLICATE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND NOT A SMELL: the two rows below are copied VERBATIM from unistd.json:42-43 — same signature spelling, same kind/linkage, same [macho] gate, same column padding. Cross-descriptor duplicates dedupe by NAME first-wins, so a byte-identical duplicate resolves to exactly ONE thing no matter which header a TU includes first (sqlite3.c includes both), while a DIVERGENT duplicate is the case that fails loud — project rule #47, a shared declaration must resolve identically per target. Keeping them literally identical IS the requirement: ANY future edit to either row must be applied to BOTH. The `library` map is declared here for the same anti-drift reason: unistd.json states `{elf: libc.so.6, macho: /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib}` EXPLICITLY, whereas an absent map inherits the LANGUAGE default (the `externLibraryByFormat` map in src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json — its `macho` row is /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib, MEASURED identical today; cited BY KEY rather than by line: the citation this replaces was a bare filename plus a line number, which named no directory and pointed at the map's `pe` row rather than the `macho` row it was arguing about — a key spelling survives both problems), so stating it makes the two descriptors agree BY STATEMENT rather than by coincidence and a later change to that default cannot silently split them. EXPORT-VERIFIED, which under the eager-import law is the load-bearing check (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT: an unexported name breaks EVERY macho binary's LOAD, not merely this header's users): both names were confirmed present in libSystem by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac ([[D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS]]) — this ships NO name that has not been seen on a real Mac. An `includes: ["unistd.h"]` transitive pull was the alternative considered and REJECTED: it would drag all 36 unistd symbols into the eager-import set of every TU that includes <sys/sysctl.h>. ★★ (3) THE MIB CONSTANTS NOW SHIP, AND THE 'WE STILL CANNOT MEASURE THE VALUES' HALF OF THIS COMMENT IS RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT. What it used to say was true of the tooling then available, not of the values: the SDK slice that work had (/tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include) carried only sys/{fcntl,file,mount,param,syslimits}.h + malloc/malloc.h, so sys/sysctl.h was simply not readable from here, and the correct call at the time was to take the fail-loud gap rather than guess a 4.4BSD-looking namespace. The gap is now closed against a REAL Mac. ★ THE CORPUS USAGE, re-measured this cycle against upstream a790e273e2 rather than inherited: `src/test1.c:9100-9104` uses the MIB-ARRAY form (`nm[0] = CTL_HW; nm[1] = HW_AVAILCPU;` then `nm[1] = HW_NCPU;`) and IS THE WHOLE CONSUMER — a scan of src/ ext/ tool/ for `CTL_[A-Z0-9_]*` and `HW_[A-Z0-9_]*` returns exactly those three names and nothing else. ⓘ A naive such scan also reports a fourth, `CTL_MAGIC`; it is a SUBSTRING of os_unix.c:391 `F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC` and not a MIB name at all — recorded so the next person who runs that grep does not re-investigate it. THE CLI REMAINS UNAFFECTED either way: sqlite3.c reaches the same kernel node through the NAME-based `sysctlbyname` above, which needs no constant, and shell.c references none. ★★ HOW THEY WERE MEASURED — 2026-08-06, on the operator's physical Mac (macOS 26.5.2 build 25F84, Apple clang 21.0.0, SDK .../MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk), BY COMPILING rather than by reading a header, with FOUR independent instruments that agree: (i) `cc -arch A -E -dM` emitted `#define CTL_HW 6`, `#define HW_NCPU 3`, `#define HW_AVAILCPU 25`; (ii) `cc -arch A -S` over `const int x = CTL_HW;` emitted `.long 6` / `.long 3` / `.long 25` into the assembly; (iii) `#pragma message` stringification expanded them to the bare tokens 6, 3, 25; (iv) a NATIVE arm64 binary and an x86_64 binary (Rosetta) both printed the same three numbers AND round-tripped `sysctl({CTL_HW,HW_NCPU}, 2, …)` through the kernel at rc=0. The SDK header text (sys/sysctl.h:193, :565, :587) agrees, but it is corroboration and not the measurement — the compiler is, because the compiler is what the value has to survive. ★★ NO PER-ARCH DIVERGENCE, AND IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the `-dM` dumps for `-arch arm64` and `-arch x86_64` were diffed over the ENTIRE CTL_*/HW_* surface — 48 lines each, `diff` rc=0, byte-identical. That measurement is WHY every row below is FLAT with no `variants`, and the check is exactly the one `_SC_PAGESIZE` in unistd.json fails (elf 30 / macho 29) and `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` fails harder (Darwin's value is not witnessed at all, so it ships elf-only). Flat here is a result, not a default. ★ THEY ARE OBJECT-LIKE `#define`s, NOT ENUMERATORS — MEASURED, since it changes how they may be declared: an enumerator never appears in `-E -dM` output and these do, and they stringify to bare decimal tokens carrying no suffix and no cast, so the C type of each expansion is plain `int` ⇒ `i32` — which is also what `sysctl`'s `int *name` parameter demands and what test1.c's `int nm[2]` stores them into. ⚠ THE FIDELITY DELTA THAT CREATES, stated rather than buried: DSS ships them in `constants`, i.e. as DECLARATIONS, so `#ifdef CTL_HW` is TRUE on real Darwin and FALSE under DSS. That is not a new decision — it is the shape every sibling already uses (LOCK_* in sys/file.json, SEEK_*/F_OK-X_OK in unistd.json, MNT_* in sys/mount.json, the whole errno family), all of them `#define`s upstream and all of them `constants` here. It is SAFE FOR THIS CORPUS BY MEASUREMENT and not by hope: a scan of the staged tree for `#ifdef`, `#ifndef` or `defined()` applied to ANY CTL_*/HW_* name returns ZERO hits. ★★ WHY THE WHOLE DOMAINS SHIP AND NOT ONLY THE THREE test1.c NEEDS — this is the sys/file.json LOCK_* discipline applied verbatim, and that file states the reason better than a restatement would: a partial constant domain, a name that exists in the real header and is absent here, compiles to a fail-loud miss on a shadowed include and is the exact trap this project keeps re-hitting. Both domains are CLOSED and CONTIGUOUS as measured, which is what makes shipping them whole a bounded act: the CTL_ top level runs 0..8 with no gaps (UNSPEC, KERN, VM, VFS, NET, DEBUG, HW, MACHDEP, USER) plus CTL_MAXID 9 as its bound and CTL_MAXNAME 12 as the MIB-array bound; the HW_ level runs 1..27 with no gaps plus HW_MAXID 28. 39 rows, every one of them read off the same two `-dM` dumps. ⓘ AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE `symbols` ARRAY ABOVE, where 'no over-ship' is a hard rule: a constant carries NO eager-import hazard. An unexported SYMBOL breaks EVERY macho binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT); an unreferenced CONSTANT costs a decode and nothing else. The two arrays are governed by different risks and correctly get different policies. ★ WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SHIP, so the omission reads as a decision: KERN_* (about 72 names, several of them literal `dummy` placeholders and several version-dependent), VM_*, USER_*, CTL_DEBUG_*, and the CTLTYPE_* type tags — each is its OWN closed domain with ZERO in-tree consumer, and a domain nobody calls is precisely where a transcription error would sit unchecked forever. Also NOT shipped, and for a different reason: the CTL_NAMES / CTL_HW_NAMES / CTL_KERN_NAMES / CTL_VM_NAMES / CTL_USER_NAMES / CTL_VFS_NAMES / CTL_DEBUG_NAMES macros, which are not integers at all but brace-initializer table literals pairing a name string with a CTLTYPE_* tag — those belong in `macros`, not here, if a consumer ever appears. A reference to anything in this paragraph fails LOUD with S0001, which is the honest gap. ⇒ D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY NARROWS from 'no constants at all' to exactly that residue plus the `struct sysctl_oid`-adjacent shapes. ★ VALUE CORRECTNESS IS WITNESSED AT RUNTIME, NOT MERELY DECLARED, and that is the whole point of the old comment's warning: a wrong MIB number still COMPILES, because this file shadows the SDK header even on a native Mac, and it would then query the wrong kernel node and return a plausible number. A value table cannot self-check — asserting CTL_HW == 6 next to a row that says 6 proves nothing. So the guard is examples/c/shipped_sysctl_mib_hw_macho, which asks the KERNEL: every MIB it addresses is cross-checked against the sysctlbyname NAME form of the same node, so a wrong CTL_HW or a wrong HW_NCPU either makes sysctl return -1 or makes the two forms disagree, and reds the example on a real Mac. ★ THE MACRO: `_SYS_SYSCTL_H_` is the include guard, the one declaration the real header unambiguously makes and that no consumer branches on. It is no longer load-bearing for shipping (the loader refuses a descriptor that declares NOTHING — shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2188-2199 — and the `symbols` above now satisfy that on their own), but it remains correct and is kept. The name follows the Darwin `_SYS_<NAME>_H_` convention MEASURED across every sibling in the slice (sys/mount.h → _SYS_MOUNT_H_, sys/param.h → _SYS_PARAM_H_, sys/file.h → _SYS_FILE_H_, sys/fcntl.h → _SYS_FCNTL_H_, sys/syslimits.h → _SYS_SYSLIMITS_H_) — the convention is measured, this specific name is INFERRED from it. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); Linux's sysctl(2) is deprecated and its MIB values differ, so an elf build must never silently pick this up.
